stage1.impression: A dark flat board standing in a clear block on cream marble; the block's lower half reads as an opaque cream slab and the curved metal sector reads as matte fabric pasted on the front, not a mirror inside acrylic. The board is a featureless dark rectangle filling the top half, and a hard-edged clipped glare patch on the floor at upper right pulls the eye off the product.

blocking_9: The stamper shard reads as a polished mirror: inside the shard (840,710,1020,790) a lum_range above 110 with dark areas below lum 100 and a bright groove streak, instead of the uniform 195 +/- 35 it is now
The acrylic reads clear: the block's lower front (520,870,780,950) shows refracted floor detail and dark edge lines, not a flat cream 176-186
The sleeve board shows a sheen falloff of at least 18 levels top to bottom instead of 35.6 to 27.6
No clipped, hard-edged reflection on the marble: clip_pct under 0.3 in (1350,200,1800,650), now 2.49
Each acrylic edge carries a continuous thin bright or dark line defining the block's silhouette against the cream floor

changes.problem: Through the front face (refraction to about 21 deg, mirror leaning back 10 deg) the shard mirrors the region near (430,-900,130) where the 700 x 180 strip sits, so the strip fills the whole mirror evenly and the grooves read as woven fabric.

evidence.measured: lum_median 194.8, p5 164.3, p95 235.8, range 71.5; x profile 204,214,212,207,203,202,197,213: a single flat light value, no dark field and no streak

changes.expected: The strip mirrors as a thin bright curved band across the shard (p95 >= 220) while the rest of the shard drops to the darker surroundings, so the shard reads as a mirror with a highlight.

changes.problem: Around the strip the shard mirrors the cream room, so even with a thinner strip the mirror's field stays light and low in contrast; a polished mirror needs something dark to reflect.

evidence.measured: lum_p5 164.3: no part of the mirror goes darker than mid-cream

change.to: matte black card 1000 x 450 mm, vertical, centred (430, -1050, 150), facing the stand, unseen by the camera, directly behind the strip as seen from the shard

changes.expected: The mirror field around the strip's streak goes near black (lum 30-90), giving the shard a black-and-silver mirror read; the black also lands in the acrylic's front faces as dark edge lines.

changes.problem: The block's lower front reads as an opaque cream slab: it refracts and internally reflects the bright floor with no dark to define the faces, so the acrylic does not read as water-clear.

evidence.measured: lum_median 185.9, r/g/b 204/184/151 (floor colour); y profile through 900-940 x: 222,212,194,171,236,184,178,176, flat in the bottom 40% of the block

change.to: two matte black cards 600 x 300 mm standing on the marble out of frame, at (-700, -200, 190) and (700, -200, 190), each turned 45 deg toward the stand, unseen by the camera

changes.expected: Dark lines and bands appear along the block's vertical end edges and lower front through refraction and TIR, the lower front gains contrast (median 130-175) and the block reads as clear glass rather than a white solid.

changes.problem: The sleeve board is one dark value: the big fill at azimuth 30 elevation 28 is mirrored evenly across the board's whole face, so it reads as a flat cutout.
changes.expected: The fill's reflection rides up the board, so the board's sheen is brightest near the top of frame and falls off toward the stand by 18-40 levels.

changes.problem: The marble mirrors the sweep as a hard-edged, clipped trapezoid at upper right that is brighter than anything on the product.

evidence.measured: lum_median 237.9, p95 247.3, clip_pct 2.49, with a sharp diagonal edge at about (1350-1800, 230-350)

changes.expected: The sweep's reflection softens into a gradient with no clipping, its peak below 240, and the product becomes the brightest-contrast thing in frame.

out_of_scope.request: Make the shard's grooves visibly finer or deeper so they diffract into a rainbow streak
out_of_scope.why: The shard's geometry and surface are fixed; the lighting changes above are what can show the grooves.
